quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Ride more slowly than usual.
Start slowing down earlier than usual.
Increase your following distance.
Talk to the passenger while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Talk to the passenger while riding.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. This makes it respond more slowly. With a passenger, ride slower than normal, slow down sooner, and increase your following distance. Always warn your passenger about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking, you should:

options.text: Release the brake until the tire grips again, then brake again.
Release the brake and only use the front brake.
Keep the brake locked until you stop.
Release the brake and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the brake locked until you stop.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while braking, do not release the brake. Keep it locked until the motorcycle stops completely.

questions.question: When it starts to rain while you are riding, what should you do?

options.text: Ride down the center of the lane.
Speed up.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of the lane has oil deposits that become slippery when wet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars. Also, slow down on wet roads.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance you should keep?

options.text: One second
Two seconds
Three seconds
Four seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds
questions.explanation: Keep a minimum following distance of two seconds. In bad weather or poor conditions, increase this to at least three seconds.

questions.question: What does a linked braking system do?

options.text: Connects the front and rear brakes so both apply when you use either brake lever.
Connects the front brake to the gear shifter to apply brakes when downshifting.
Connects the rear brake to a foot control.
Connects the rear brake to a handlebar switch.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connects the front and rear brakes so both apply when you use either brake lever.
questions.explanation: A linked braking system connects the front and rear brakes. When you use either brake lever, both brakes apply. Read your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: How often should you check your motorcycle's hydraulic fluid?

options.text: Every day
Every week
Every year
Before every ride

questions.correctAnswerText: Every week
questions.explanation: Check hydraulic fluids and coolants at least once a week before you ride. Regular pre-ride checks help keep your motorcycle safe.

questions.question: Compared to car headlights, motorcycle headlights are:

options.text: Usually more powerful.
Usually the same power.
Usually less powerful.
Usually larger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually less powerful.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle headlights are smaller and less powerful than car headlights.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, why should you NOT move to the far side of your lane?

options.text: It discourages the driver from cutting back too early.
It encourages the driver to cut back too early.
It encourages the driver to pass as quickly as possible.
It encourages other drivers to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It encourages the driver to cut back too early.
questions.explanation: Moving to the far side of your lane could encourage the passing driver to return to your lane before it is safe. Stay in the center of your lane when being passed.

questions.question: When stopping, what is the best technique?

options.text: Grab at the front brake lever quickly.
Keep your knees against the gas tank and look ahead.
Increase pressure on the rear brake gradually.
Use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank and look ahead.
questions.explanation: For best braking, apply the brakes smoothly and firmly. As weight moves forward, the front wheel gets more grip, so increase front brake pressure while reducing rear brake pressure. Keep your knees against the tank and eyes forward to stay in a straight line.

questions.question: When you stop your motorcycle, which gear should you stay in?

options.text: First gear
Neutral
Fifth gear
Any gear

questions.correctAnswerText: First gear
questions.explanation: Downshift through the gears as you slow down. Stay in first gear when stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: How do you do maximum straight-line braking?

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use the rear brake first, then the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
Use both brakes at the same time and lock the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: Maximum straight-line braking happens when you use both the front and rear brakes together without locking either wheel.

questions.question: Riding clothes should protect you from all of the following except:

options.text: Sunburn.
Windburn.
Chapped lips.
Dehydration.

questions.correctAnswerText: Chapped lips.
questions.explanation: Your riding clothes should protect you from sunburn, windburn, rain, dehydration, cold, and motorcycle parts. They should also help protect you if you crash.

questions.question: Fatigue can be increased by:

options.text: Stopping frequently.
Riding in cool weather.
Being comfortable during your ride.
Starting a ride late in the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in cool weather.
questions.explanation: To fight fatigue, dress for bad weather like wind and rain. Ride no more than six hours a day and take a break every two hours. Do not use stimulants because you may feel very tired when they wear off.

questions.question: The middle of the lane usually has an oily strip. You should:

options.text: Avoid the oily strip when it is raining.
Ride only on the oily strip for better traction.
Avoid the entire center portion of the lane.
Not worry about oil or other items in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the oily strip when it is raining.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars and trucks builds up in the center of lanes. When the road is dry, this strip usually has enough traction for motorcycles. The strip is narrow enough that you can ride on either side and still be in the center lane.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders should:

options.text: Wear hearing protection at all times to prevent hearing damage.
Wear hearing protection only on long rides.
Not wear hearing protection because it blocks horns and sirens.
Not wear hearing protection if they use a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear hearing protection at all times to prevent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can cause permanent hearing damage, even with a full-face helmet. Ear plugs protect your hearing while still letting you hear important sounds like horns and sirens.

questions.question: If a passing vehicle's wind blast hits you, you will have the most room to react if you are riding:

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the center portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Riding in the middle of your lane gives you the most space to recover if a wind blast disrupts your control.

questions.question: Riding in the center of the lane:

options.text: Makes others less able to see you.
Is always safe when approaching intersections.
Discourages other vehicles from sharing your lane.
Should be avoided if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Discourages other vehicles from sharing your lane.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need a full lane to ride safely. It is dangerous and usually illegal for a motorcycle and another vehicle to share the same lane. Riding in the center of your lane discourages others from trying to share it.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn by turning only your head. Keep your knees against the gas tank for better balance. Keep your arms slightly bent when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: To slow down before turning, you should:

options.text: Shift into neutral.
Pull in the clutch and use both brakes.
Apply the rear brake only.
Close the throttle and apply both brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the throttle and apply both brakes.
questions.explanation: Before you turn, slow down by closing the throttle and applying both brakes if needed.

questions.question: When being passed, do not move to the far side of your lane because:

options.text: The passing vehicle may re-enter your lane too early.
You may prevent another vehicle from passing you.
The side near the passing vehicle is better.
You are more likely to feel a wind blast on the far side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The passing vehicle may re-enter your lane too early.
questions.explanation: When being passed, do not move to the far side of your lane. This might tempt the other driver to return to your lane before they have enough space to do so safely.
